title: SPIN Selling - Discovery Call
subtitle: Framework
useWhen: You're talking too much and pitching too early on discovery calls. You leave without fully understanding what the prospect actually needs and they leave without feeling heard.
howToUse: Neil Rackham analysed 35,000 sales calls over 12 years and found that high-value sales are won through questions, not pitches. SPIN replaces pitching with structured questioning: Situation questions establish context, Problem questions surface pain, Implication questions show the cost of inaction, Need-Payoff questions let the prospect articulate why they need your solution in their own words. The prospect who convinces themselves is the easiest to close. Skipping Implication is what makes a close feel pushed rather than earned. A prospect who says out loud why the problem matters will defend that far harder than any pitch could.
steps: Prepare 3 questions for each SPIN stage before every call use the prompt below.
Ask all Situation questions first, then move to Problem. Never pitch before Need- Payoff
After the call, paste the transcript into AI and ask it to identify which SPIN stage each exchange covered.
The goal of a discovery call is for the prospect to articulate the problem and the value of solving it not for you to explain your product. Turn every sales call into a structured insight session
promptBody:
Act as a B2B sales coach using Neil Rackham's SPIN Selling.
I am selling       :  [YOUR PRODUCT OR SERVICE]
Prospect role    :  [JOB TITLE AND INDUSTRY]
Known context :  [WHAT YOU KNOW ABOUT THEM ALREADY]
Generate 3 strong questions for each SPIN stage:
SITUATION       :  Understand their current state and setup
PROBLEM         :  Surface the pain they may not have named
IMPLICATION  :  Show the cost and consequence of not solving it
NEED-PAYOFF :  Let them articulate the value of solving it
#Make questions feel like natural conversation.  #Avoid yes/no questions.
Favour open questions.  #Sequence them so each stage flows into the next.

proTip:
Spend 70% of your call on Implication questions  that is where urgency is created.
Most salespeople rush to Need-Payoff without building enough implication first. A
prospect who hasn't felt the pain of inaction will not feel urgency to act.
